main_body: desert building with flat roof parapet, dome, and brick front wall
top_band: light sandy tan roof surface with parapet border and turquoise dome, rows 2-33
evidence: Rows 2-33 form the flat sandy roof enclosed by a parapet wall (with inner drop shadow on top/left at rows 4-5) and topped with a turquoise dome. Row 32 is a bright front-edge highlight, row 33 is the lower parapet lip, and rows 34-35 form a dark eave shadow over the brick front wall (rows 34-63) which has an inset arched doorway and window.

style.evidence: The brick blocks and sandy roof are much larger, simpler, and more geometric than the intricately shaded small stones and roof tiles of the Beodeul references. While it uses material-toned outlines and some pixel speckle, the brick mortar is a uniform grid and the door/arch framing is blocky and repetitive, making it look noticeably flatter and less dense than the reference buildings.
